messages:
Rachel: Quick follow-up from the API GW / Edge RFC — need to land a concrete proposal for streaming resume semantics + how it affects SLAs. Short thread to capture constraints and recommended defaults.

Jaspreet: high level constraints from runtime: we can checkpoint KV-state per connection but it costs ~2-5MB per active resume point. TTLs matter.

Tim: from gateway side: we can't hold sockets forever. Prefer a resume token the client can present so we don't need long-lived sessions on the GW.

Anika: ops note: any resume approach must not blow memory when traffic spikes. We have to plan eviction and a predictable failure mode (return 409 or 410).

Rachel: agreed. Tradeoffs: 1) GW keeps soft state (cheap, fast resume), 2) GW returns opaque resume token and runtime stores state, 3) fully client-driven replay. Which do we pick as default? :thinking:

Jaspreet: technically easiest and most robust for latency is (2): runtime stores KV cache + sequence pointer, GW issues token that references runtime slot. But runtime needs TTL and an eviction policy. If runtime is multi-tenant we must isolate memory accounting per customer.

Tim: lean towards (2) but require token to be self-validating so we avoid extra lookup on every new attach. Proposal: token = base64({runtime_id, slot_id, expiry, hmac}). On attach GW validates hmac and routes resume attach directly to runtime instance (by runtime_id). If slot expired, return 410 (expired).

Anika: what about hedging and failover? If the runtime instance is down, we should allow fallback to a "restart-from-prefix" mode where we replay client prefix to a different runtime instance. That has cost but keeps availability.

Jaspreet: replay has to be bounded. Suggest a two-mode resume: fast-resume (slot present) and replay-resume (client must resend last N tokens). We limit N based on model context window and memory budget (e.g., 1024 tokens).

Rachel: example token format in RFC draft: ```resume_token=eyJydW50aWQiOiJyLXIxIiwic2xvdCI6IjEwMDMiLCJleHAiOjE2MTAwMCwiaG1hYyI6ImFiYyJ9``` which decodes to {runtime,slot,expiry,hmac}. We validate expiry on GW to short-circuit obvious failures.

Tim: routing detail — GW must carry the request's routing headers when switching to runtime attach: X-Request-Id, X-Customer-Id, X-Auth-Tier. Also a small window for TLS session reuse if possible.

Anika: SLA implications: if resume succeeds we should count latency from original request start for SLOs? That skews numbers. Better: mark resumed responses with metadata so SLO dashboards exclude resumed latency or track them separately.

Jaspreet: agreed. Emit trace tag resume=true and original_start_ts. Observability: we need per-route counters: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_replay.

Rachel: idempotency/side-effects question: streaming requests can include tool calls. Resume must be safe w.r.t side-effects. Options: 1) disallow resume for non-idempotent streams; 2) require Explicit-Resume-Allowed header + Idempotency-Key for side-effecting steps. Thoughts?

Tim: We can't rely on clients to be correct. Gateway should reject resume when stream contains stateful tool calls unless caller provided an Idempotency-Key and we validate at runtime. Default: resume disabled if tools used.

Anika: we also need clear errors for clients: 409 (conflict) when resume token mismatches, 410 (gone) when expired, 412 (precondition failed) when requested resume not allowed due to tools/side-effects.

Jaspreet: runtime responsibilities: allocate slot, persist minimal KV checkpoint, accept reattach with token, or reject. Provide API: POST /resume/attach {token, headers} -> 200 + websocket upgrade or 4xx. Also: DELETE /resume/slot/{id} on explicit close.

Tim: GW responsibilities: issue token TTL short by default (e.g., 60s), accept reattach, validate hmac locally, route attach to runtime. If runtime not available, gateway can return 503 and optionally trigger replay path if allowed.

Anika: cost model: add a small per-minute slot charge for Dedicated customers, or include in runtime CPU billing. Need new billing event: resume.slot.hour. Ops will need dashboard for slot usage.

Rachel: outstanding edge cases: multiregion routing when runtime_id points to a region that changed. Should support region remap with safe fallback. Also ensure tokens are rotated with KMS keys.

Jaspreet: security: token HMAC must be signed with per-cluster key. Keys rotate -> tokens include key_id so GW can validate or reject older tokens post-rotation.

Tim: quick implementation plan: (a) GW token generator + validator (small PR), (b) runtime slot API and eviction TTL + metrics (Jaspreet), (c) client SDK support for resume attach & error handling (DevEx).

Rachel: action items: I will open a PR with the design doc + sample token spec. @Jaspreet please sketch runtime API surface and memory accounting. @Tim add gateway header routing & error codes. @Anika add billing/monitoring tickets.

ingress-bot: Deploy scheduled: edge-canary v2.14 -> will include token-validator library. :shipit:

Rachel: thanks everyone — keeping resume off by default for streams with tools is the safe default. We'll propose (2) as default for text-only streaming with 60s TTL and replay-capable fallback. I'll tag the RFC PR by EOD. :thumbsup:
